clue.text: Snag with clutch

definitions.meaning: a snag or hidden drawback in a deal
to clutch is to grab hold of something

explanation.definitionFit: A hidden drawback is a snag, and seizing hold of something with the hands is to clutch it.

clue.text: French article in support of very bad journal

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad or dreadful
le is the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A French newspaper item propping up a dreadful magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'in support of' puts LE below CHRONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical record of events, like a diary or journal kept over time.

clue.text: Our mist swirling? This is getting away from it!

definitions.text: This is getting away from it!

indicators.note: the words 'Our mist' are swirled about into a new letter order

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker escaping the swirling fog at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' rearranges OURMIST; the exclamatory definition plays on the phrase 'getting away from it all', meaning taking a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel for pleasure is the industry of escape from daily routine.

clue.text: Keep secret cash, say?

definitions.meaning: to keep something secret is to conceal it
cash sounds like cache, a stash or store, which also means to stow away out of sight

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works through sound: 'cash' is said like 'cache', and to cache something is to stow it away.
explanation.definitionFit: Concealing something keeps it secret, and to cache valuables is to stow them out of sight.

clue.text: Smoother means of raising aircraft

parts.note: a jack is a device for lifting a car
a plane is an aircraft

explanation.surface: A gentler way of lifting a plane off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoother' is a tool, not a comparative: a carpenter's plane smooths wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker's plane for rough work evens out timber surfaces, so it is a tool that smooths.

clue.text: This means of punishment can produce a lesion, can't it?

indicators.note: the letters of 'a lesion, can't it' are worked to produce a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A whip asks rhetorically whether it can leave a wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' rearranges ALESIONCANTIT; the whole clue also describes the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: This knotted many-thonged whip was used for flogging sailors and prisoners.

clue.text: Man manipulated on board

parts.note: a chess piece of the lowest rank is a 'man' moved about on the board, and also a person used by others

explanation.definitionFit: The humblest chess piece is a man moved around the board, and figuratively a person used as a tool.

clue.text: Talk over desert deliveries from above

definitions.note: plural phrase for a singular noun, read as a kind of delivery

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to air views is to talk about them
to desert friends is to drop them

explanation.surface: A discussion about abandoning shipments falling from the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' puts AIR above DROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies dropped by parachute from aircraft come down from the sky.

clue.text: Racecourse record doctor's overturned

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for the doctor's is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor; with the 's it gives MOS

explanation.surface: A doctor's vinyl disc flipped over at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns MOS into SOM. EPSOM Downs is a famous English racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom Downs in Surrey stages the Derby horse race.

clue.text: Gathering in stock?

parts.note: stock here is livestock, and herding cattle together is a gathering of them

explanation.definitionFit: Herding cattle together on a ranch collects the livestock into one place.

clue.text: Great spread of people in favour of time-share?

parts.note: pros are people in favour of something; one such supporter is a pro
a life is a span of time, as in 'the time of my life'
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: Fans of holiday time-share schemes spreading widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time-share' is two pieces: 'time' gives LIFE and 'share' gives RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid multiplication across a wide area is a spread on a large scale.

clue.text: Just before two, perhaps, a road's shortened

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word two is only a possible version, its letters jumbled

parts.note: RD is the short form of road, and with the 's gives RDS

explanation.surface: A road abbreviated in a timetable showing something just before two o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TWO into TOW. 'Just before two' looks like a time, as in 'towards two', but only 'Just before' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Approaching a point in time means coming close to it, a little ahead of it.

clue.text: Man in a line-out

indicators.note: out suggests the word line is disordered, put out of its usual order

explanation.surface: A rugby player throwing in at a line-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LINE. A line-out restarts play in rugby when the ball goes into touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name stands for a man in crosswords.

clue.text: Pen of poet

definitions.meaning: Ezra ... was an American modernist poet

explanation.definitionFit: An enclosure for stray animals is a pen, and Ezra the American modernist wrote verse.

clue.text: A strange variety of lily

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd kind of lily.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum lily is a well-known garden plant with a white spathe.

clue.text: Fellow is not commonly timid and weak

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of 'is not'

explanation.surface: A man who is not, as some say, shy and feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being faint-hearted is being timid, and a feeble effort or sound is weak.

clue.text: Hip replaced with aluminium requires bottle!

indicators.note: the letters of hip are placed again in a new order

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A hip replacement made of aluminium needs a drink!
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges HIP into PHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass vial for medicine is a little bottle.

clue.text: Mate joining vessel's company

parts.note: a mate is a companion
a ship is a vessel; the 's is absorbed

explanation.surface: A ship's mate joining the crew of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping someone company means being with them, as friends are together.

clue.text: Acrobatic turn that makes an impression on field

definitions.meaning: a sideways handspring rotating the body like a spoke

definitions.text: that makes an impression on field
definitions.meaning: the wheel of a farm wagon leaves a rut pressed into the ground

explanation.definitionFit: A gymnast's sideways handspring turns like a spinning spoke, and a farm wagon's wheel presses ruts into the soil.

clue.text: American leader in agreement with governor

parts.note: concert means agreement, as in 'acting in concert'
a master is one who governs or controls

explanation.surface: A US politician who sees eye to eye with the state governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American leader' suggests a politician, but it is the US term for an orchestra's lead violinist.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage the principal first violinist who leads the orchestra holds this title.

clue.text: Company short, perhaps, of soldiers in numbers

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word short is only one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A military company running short of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges SHORT into HORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman army units of several hundred troops were cohorts, so they are soldiers in bulk.

clue.text: Trill by foreign piper is for the tourist

parts.note: tr is the musical notation abbreviation for trill

indicators.note: foreign suggests the word piper is made strange, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A trill played by an overseas bagpiper entertains a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges PIPER into IPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A day visitor on an outing is a holidaymaker or sightseer.

clue.text: Sound of merriment from low fence

definitions.meaning: a sunken fence or ditch bounding a park, invisible from the house

explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is written as two repeated syllables, and a sunken boundary ditch in English estate gardens has the same name.

clue.text: 28 right for this pigeon?

parts.note: the answer to 28 across is residence, which means home

explanation.surface: A bird with a right to a home.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 28 across, whose answer means HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: A homing pigeon trained to fly back to its loft is called a homer.

clue.text: Fleet attack to seize power

indicators.note: the attack takes hold of power by closing around it

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A navy squadron launching an assault to grab power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' looks like a navy but is the adjective meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet of foot means swift and quick-moving.

clue.text: Scene of contest with women?

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete

explanation.surface: The sight of a competition involving women.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene laid out before you is the outlook or sight you see.

clue.text: Passionless, being one hundred years of age

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred
old is used of age in years, as in 'ten years old'

explanation.surface: A centenarian who has lost all ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking warmth or feeling is chilly and unemotional.

clue.text: Distress felt by guitarists

definitions.meaning: a ridge across a guitar's neck, felt under the fingers

explanation.definitionFit: To worry anxiously is to be in distress, and guitarists press strings against the raised metal bars on the neck.

clue.text: Wireless pioneer from Minorca

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is made out of the letters of Minorca, rearranged

explanation.surface: An early radio pioneer who came from a Balearic island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges MINORCA; Guglielmo MARCONI pioneered radio telegraphy.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo was the Italian inventor credited with developing radio telegraphy, the old 'wireless'.

clue.text: Brawl that is a trouble in the Cotswolds!

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or brawl
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A fight that causes trouble in rural English villages.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds, hills in western England, are famous sheep-farming country, so the trouble there is a disease of sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: This fatal brain disease of sheep plagues farmers in sheep country.

clue.text: Dense rice mixture in home

indicators.note: the words 'Dense rice' are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Stodgy rice mixed up at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' rearranges DENSERICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling or house where someone lives is their home.

clue.text: Pretty, rolling section of mountainous area

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a lovely undulating mountain landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: TYROL is an Alpine region of western Austria and northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: This Alpine region of Austria and Italy is high mountain country.
